scope: Only three pre-existing independent lower passages X0/X1/X2. No connection to upper crossing reaches and no new underground topology.
width: 2+2*sqrt(original lower-reach mean discharge) metres; assumed rectangular conduit
height: Adopted maximum lower water stage plus1m freeboard
bed: Original adopted channel profile at the three equal-length section centres, including X2 cosine-squared lowering
storage: Each section has width*length/3 free-surface area up to its roof, then width squared surcharge storage. This slot is an explicit incompressible pressure-storage approximation, not a pressure-wave solver.
flow: Signed quasi-steady Darcy-Weisbach head-loss law. Effective wet area is limited by donor head above the higher adjoining floor; full hydraulic diameter is retained as an explicit partial-fill approximation. Coupled implicit conservative pair exchanges iterate to a common network solution and are donor bounded.
forcing: Divert original background local runoff whose original receiver path first encounters one of the three lower reaches into that passage upstream compartment, subtracting the identical per-cell load from its original pond. Route entire contributing reach load to entrance as an explicit spatial lumping assumption. Downstream section exchanges with the original next-node pond, with finite donor water and reverse flow.
initial: All new conduit sections start empty. No priming water is invented. Existing105 state and total background inputs preserved.
thermal: Subsurface water remains liquid; no new underground heat budget. Existing surface ice, snow, glacier and frost laws retained.
solid: Existing23022 reach sediment and bed evolution continue. These three background passages have no imported sediment source or new erosion law.
control: Closed passage exchange0 retains the same background diversion and stores the water; absent module preserves previous engine exactly.
limits: Not an observed conduit geometry or calibrated roughness
